READING

**Costs that are identical under both courses**

The GBP 27,072 crossing burden (10 technicians × ~28 excess remakes × GBP 96) is unavoidable regardless of timing. It cancels out when comparing the two and need not affect the decision.

**The one large fixed charge that is not shared: the GBP 44,000 overtime**

KIRKBANE commits to this unconditionally. AVENSWOOD does not spend it. That sum becomes the effective hurdle: for AVENSWOOD to lose on cost, its incremental liabilities must collectively exceed GBP 44,000.

**Estimating cross-system remake exposure under AVENSWOOD**

The pilot gives a calibration point: 2 technicians on the new system, 10 remaining on Kessendale, 4 months, 40 crossing remakes. I use the interaction model, where the risk scales with the product of technicians on each side, since a crossing remake requires one foot in each system.

| Phase | Duration | New × Old pairs | Rate (remakes/pair/month) | Remakes |
|-------|----------|-----------------|--------------------------|---------|
| Jan–Apr 2027 | 3 months | 3 × 9 = 27 | 0.5* | 40.5 |
| Apr–Jul 2027 | 3 months | 6 × 6 = 36 | 0.5 | 54.0 |
| Jul–Oct 2027 | 3 months | 9 × 3 = 27 | 0.5 | 40.5 |
| **Total** | | | | **~135** |

*Derived from pilot: 40 remakes ÷ (20 pairs × 4 months) = 0.5.

135 × GBP 96 = **GBP 12,960**.

A flat model (10 remakes per month × 9 months = 90 remakes) gives GBP 8,640. A pessimistic model that doubles the pilot rate gives ~GBP 25,920. All three are well below GBP 44,000. The GBP 44,000 overtime must be the deciding financial variable.

**AVENSWOOD incremental costs vs. KIRKBANE savings**

| Item | AVENSWOOD extra cost | KIRKBANE extra cost |
|------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Overtime | — | GBP 44,000 |
| Cross-system remakes | GBP 9,000–26,000 | ~GBP 0 |
| Dual library admin | Unquantified but bounded | — |
| **Net** | **GBP 9,000–26,000** | **GBP 44,000** |

AVENSWOOD is GBP 18,000–35,000 cheaper even under adverse remake assumptions.

**Practice-relationship risk**

Under KIRKBANE, with 10 of 12 technicians on 11.4% simultaneously, the lab-wide remake rate visible to practices spikes to roughly:

(2 × 3.4 + 10 × 11.4) / 12 ≈ **10.1%**

All forty practices see this in the same month. That is a 3.3-fold deterioration from the 3.1% they expect, arriving without differentiation across the client base. Practices that notice it together may act together.

Under AVENSWOOD, the worst-case lab-wide rate (first wave, 3 technicians at 11.4%):

(2 × 3.4 + 3 × 11.4 + 9 × 3.1) / 14 ≈ **4.8%**

A mild, partially masked rise affecting a subset of practices at any one time. Practices on the unaffected portion of the bench see nothing unusual.

**Dual library period**

Nine months of two libraries is a real administrative burden and the shade-consistency risk is genuine. However, the pilot has already demonstrated this for four months without apparent catastrophic failure, and the 40-remake figure already captures much of the material consequence. The library overhead is bounded and temporary.

**Timeline adequacy**

AVENSWOOD completes the transition on 2027-10-04; KIRKBANE on 2027-12-04. Both sit roughly eight months inside the 2028-06-30 Kessendale end-of-support date. Neither course is pressured by the deadline.

**Summary**

KIRKBANE pays a firm GBP 44,000 to concentrate and shorten the pain. AVENSWOOD avoids that payment, spreads the quality impact thinly across the practice base, and incurs cross-system remake costs that the pilot data bounds well below GBP 44,000 even under generous assumptions. The financial and the client-relationship arguments point the same way.

---

CALL
AVENSWOOD

GROUNDS
The GBP 44,000 overtime that KIRKBANE commits unconditionally exceeds every defensible estimate of AVENSWOOD's cross-system remake liability, and AVENSWOOD also prevents all forty practices from experiencing a simultaneous quality deterioration.
